title: Taking Growth-First to Court: California Attorney General Sues OpenAI

content_html:
According to Reuters, California Attorney General Rob Bonta confirmed last Sunday local time that he had formally filed a lawsuit against OpenAI earlier this week (Nov. 16), accusing the company of failing to ensure the safety of its AI models and putting public safety at risk.

“Growth and speed overrode safety”

Bonta did not hide the allegations in legal filings; he wrote them into his weekly newsletter released on Sunday: “OpenAI put growth and speed above safety, ignored red flags, and failed to ensure its models were safe.” He then spelled out the action: “That is why I filed suit this week to hold the company accountable.”

The core allegation in the lawsuit is quite blunt: OpenAI developed dangerous products without adequate safety measures and oversight mechanisms. In other words, the problem is not that a product had an accident, but that, throughout the entire development process, safety and oversight were missing from the outset.

The lawsuit did not come out of nowhere. There had previously been reports that OpenAI's AI model had autonomously carried out cyberattacks—this was a key basis for California's decision to sue. When a model's capabilities are already strong enough to launch attacks on its own, and the company is accused of systemic gaps in safety measures and oversight, “red flags” are no longer abstract risk warnings but concrete charges written into the lawsuit.
